_note: V1.5a re-authored anti_corruption_agency onto effects.society, and the reason is booked in ROADMAP.md's V1.5 decomposition rather than discovered here. S7 priced corruption as `other_revenue_pct_gdp: 0.1` -- recovered money -- because there was no corruption quantity for a law to move, so the law described its own SIDE EFFECT and called it the mechanism. The day the quantity exists that channel is wrong twice over: it says fighting corruption is a revenue measure, and it leaves the level untouched, so the agency this law establishes changes nothing about how well the state delivers anything. The recovered revenue is not modelled rather than modelled at zero -- a receipts line for one law would be the corporate-receipts channel V1.4b cut, arriving through a side door. Same treatment `immigration_tightening` in social.json is owed at V1.5b.

laws.name: Proportional Representation Act
laws.summary: Elect the assembly by national proportional list with a 5% threshold, ending the majoritarian system. Every party's seats come to match its vote.

laws.name: Two-Round Voting Act
laws.summary: Elect the assembly in single-member contests decided over two rounds, so the largest party governs alone rather than by coalition.

laws.name: Anti-Corruption Agency Act
laws.summary: Establish an independent agency to investigate public corruption.

laws._note: V1.5a, and the only NEW content the session authors. Without it the positive half of society_constants.CORRUPTION_MAX is unreachable in play -- an anti-corruption law can only ever push a clean state cleaner -- so tools/society_probe.gd would be sweeping CORRUPTION_DELIVERY_BETA against a saturated level the game cannot produce, which is V1.3f's measuring-the-wrong-state error in the file written to avoid it. Priced on potential_growth_pct rather than on a spending line because src/core/law.gd refuses effects.society beside effects.spending_pct_gdp: emergency powers get things BUILT, and what they cost is how well everything else is delivered. It may not touch a spending line and does not need to.
laws.name: Emergency Procurement Powers Act
laws.summary: Suspend competitive tendering so public projects can be awarded directly.

laws.name: Regional Devolution Act
laws.summary: Devolve spending powers over infrastructure to regional government.

laws.name: Public Broadcasting Reform Act
laws.summary: Guarantee the broadcaster's editorial independence in statute.

laws.name: Broadcasting Oversight Act
laws.summary: Put licensing and editorial standards under a ministerial board.

laws.name: Emergency Broadcasting Powers
laws.summary: Suspend licences and vet coverage while public order is at risk.

laws.name: Lobbying Transparency Act
laws.summary: Require public disclosure of lobbying contacts with ministers.

laws.name: Judicial Appointments Reform Act
laws.summary: Give the executive the deciding voice in naming the constitutional bench.

laws.name: Judicial Review (Limitation) Act
laws.summary: Narrow the classes of statute the constitutional court may hear at all.

laws.name: Judicial Tenure Act
laws.summary: Lower the retirement age for sitting judges and reopen every seat on the bench.

laws.name: Judicial Independence Act
laws.summary: Entrench judicial tenure and widen who may refer a bill to the court.

laws.name: Regional List Voting Act
laws.summary: Elect the assembly by regional proportional lists with a five per cent threshold.

laws.name: Mixed-Member Voting Act
laws.summary: Half the seats single-member, half from regional lists, so each area keeps a name and the votes still count.

laws.name: First-Past-The-Post Act
laws.summary: Single-member constituencies decided on one round, so the largest party can govern alone.

laws.name: Lower Thresholds Act
laws.summary: Cut the proportional threshold from five per cent to three, so the small parties keep their seats.

laws.name: Citizens' Initiative Act
laws.summary: A petition of a million voters forces a binding referendum on any law the assembly has passed.

laws.name: Assembly Reduction Act
laws.summary: Cut the chamber by a fifth: fewer seats, less pay, a smaller staff bill.

laws.name: Civil Service Reform Act
laws.summary: Open every senior post to outside competition, on fixed terms.

laws.name: Beneficial Ownership Register
laws.summary: A public register naming the person behind every company and every trust.

laws.name: Whistleblower Protection Act
laws.summary: Protected disclosure channels, and the dismissal burden reversed onto the employer.

laws.name: Freedom of Information Act
laws.summary: A statutory right to ask for the government's documents, and actually receive them.

laws.name: Electoral Commission Act
laws.summary: Independent boundary reviews and campaign-finance enforcement, under one commission.

laws.name: Euro Preparation Act
laws.summary: Set a target date and a convergence plan for adopting the single currency.

laws.name: Bench Expansion Act
laws.summary: Enlarge the constitutional court, and let the government name the new seats.
